title: Add PMU-based sampling counters and continuous-batch simulator harness
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Adds PMU-backed cycle counters and a continuous-batching simulator/harness for reproducing live request distributions. Exposes per-core ring buffer export for timeline analysis and integrates NVTX markers for scheduler windows.
commits: b3e4a21: lightweight per-core ring buffer and exporter hooks
c7d9f30: NVTX scheduler annotations added and gated behind PERF_BUILD
d2a7b56: continuous-batch simulator with request trace replay support
e5f1a11: timeline CSV exporter and visualization helpers
f9b2c88: add integration test and CI perf pipeline job
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently need a low-overhead, system-level signal for per-token cycles to attribute runtime overhead between kernel execution, scheduling, and blocking I/O. Existing high-res counters (nvtx and software timers) are useful but insufficient to correlate CPU-side stalls and kernel timings at the per-core level under high-concurrency continuous batching.

Summary of changes: Adds a PMU-backed sampler (runtime/telemetry/pmu_sampler.*) that uses perf_event_open to record core cycle and instructions-retired counters with a lightweight sampling loop and per-core ring buffers. The sampler is opt-in (enabled via PERF_BUILD and runtime flag) and drains into an in-memory ring buffer exposed to user-space exporter hooks. We added a small, single-file continuous-batch simulator (tools/batch_sim/continuous_sim.cpp) that can replay recorded request arrival traces and exercise scheduler policies and batching heuristics deterministically. An exporter (perf/exporters/timeline_csv_exporter.py) converts ring buffer samples + NVTX annotations into a timeline CSV compatible with existing perf dashboards and a simple post-processing script to drive Speedscope/Perfetto. NVTX annotations were added around scheduler windows to make the scheduler batching lifecycle visible in traces.

Design notes: The PMU sampler aims for minimal overhead by: 1) sampling at a coarse frequency tuned per workload, 2) using mmap'd ring buffers to avoid syscalls on record-forward path, and 3) compressing sample payloads to 16 bytes (timestamp, core, sample-type bits, value). The ring buffer API is intentionally small (push/poll/drain) so it can be reused by other telemetry producers in the runtime. The continuous-batch simulator supports trace replay with adjustable QPS, jitter models, and per-request sequence length distributions to approximate production traffic during perf runs.

Performance impact: On a representative generator (concurrent clients=64, mean seq=256, model=redwood-7b-quant), enabling the sampler at a 1ms sample interval added ~0.6% median per-token CPU overhead and produced stable cycle attribution samples. Using the simulator we reproduced a 7-12% median per-token latency regression in a scheduler path when a misconfigured batching window caused frequent micro-batching; the NVTX + PMU trace made the root cause (frequent wakeups + context-switch stalls) obvious.

Tests and CI: Added an integration test (tests/perf/pmu_sampler_integration_test.cpp) that runs the sampler in a controlled environment and validates ring-buffer exports and exporter parsing. CI: perf-pipeline job added to infra/ci/perf-pipeline.yml that runs the simulator with a small trace and validates timeline export. The initial CI run failed due to missing CAP_SYS_ADMIN in container; we updated the perf CI image and reran — final CI status: pass.

Files/areas touched: runtime telemetry and scheduler, a new tooling harness under tools/batch_sim, a small Python exporter, docs and example traces, and CI perf job. Changes are mostly additive; scheduler NVTX annotations are guarded by a preprocessor define so runtime behavior is unchanged when PERF_BUILD is off.

Review conversation (high-level):
- Evelyn Zhang: "Can the sampler be made lock-free on the hot path to avoid contention when we have many cores? Also please add a length-bounded drain to avoid OOM in pathological traces."
- Maya (author): "Sampler uses per-core buffers and mmap'd ring semantics; hot path avoids locks. Added a bounded drain and a configuration option (max-buffer-events) with a reasonable default."
- Samuel Park: "Simulator is great — minor nit: make the default trace rate conservative in CI to avoid flaky runs."
- Maya: "Default rate reduced and CI uses a tiny synthetic trace."
- Irfan Khan: "Will this interact poorly with Dedicated nodes where we can't enable perf in some environments?"
- Maya: "Sampler is opt-in and disabled in Private/installer builds by default; docs updated in docs/perf/pmu-bench.md."

Known limitations and next steps: PMU sampling requires elevated privileges in some environments; the docs call out how to enable CAP_SYS_ADMIN or use a privileged CI image. Future work: add kernel-side eBPF glue to correlate user-space PIDs with hardware events (follow-up ENG-4180), and integrate a lightweight visual dashboard that surfaces per-route cycle attribution in Redwood Console.

Related work: references ENG-4123 (follow-up to earlier lightweight counters work), ties into perf-dashboard exports added in previous PRs but provides a lower-level signal better suited for CPU-bound regressions.

Merge: Squash-merged after reviewers approved and CI passed.
